header.title: Canada's capital-deepening cycle lifts potential growth and Canadian assets

s01_bottom_line.text: Morgan Stanley argues Canada's potential growth could rise from ~1.5% to 1.7% by end-decade and reach 2% in the 2030s, driven by productivity, efficiency and capital deployment, supported by abundant capital (pension assets 158% of GDP), a growing working-age population (+5% by 2040), and a capex cycle in which utilities, transport, mining and energy are ~61% of planned 2026 capex. ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate⟩
The payoff should be faster growth, stronger corporate earnings and a more constructive outlook for Canadian assets, including a CAD strengthening to 1.36 from ~1.39. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩

If the capital cycle broadens from structures/engineering into machinery, software and IP and productivity spreads, Canadian corporate earnings and the Canadian dollar could benefit; the article does not quantify the earnings effect.
